question:
Education is kept under which list of the Indian Constitution?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Government list
State list
Concurrent list
Union list
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Concurrent list

Explanation:
Education is placed under the Concurrent List of the Indian Constitution, as mentioned in the Seventh Schedule (Article 246). Subjects in the Concurrent List can be legislated upon by both the Union and State governments. In case of a conflict between laws made by the Centre and a State, the law made by Parliament prevails (Article 254). Originally, education was part of the State List, but the 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976) shifted it to the Concurrent List, enabling the Centre to standardize education policies nationwide.

Extra Facts:
The Concurrent List contains 52 subjects, including education, marriage & divorce, criminal procedure, forests, and labor welfare. The State List has 61 subjects, while the Union List has 97. The Right to Education Act (RTE), 2009, enacted by the Centre, guarantees free and compulsory education to children aged 6-14, enforcing the fundamental right under Article 21A.

question_hi:
शिक्षा को भारतीय संविधान में किस सूची के अंतर्गत रखा गया है?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi: सरकारी सूची
राज्य सूची
समवर्ती सूची
संघ सूची
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है समवर्ती सूची

Explanation:
शिक्षा को भारतीय संविधान की समवर्ती सूची (Concurrent List) में रखा गया है, जो सातवीं अनुसूची के अनुच्छेद 246 में उल्लिखित है। समवर्ती सूची में शामिल विषयों पर केंद्र और राज्य दोनों कानून बना सकते हैं। यदि केंद्र और राज्य के कानूनों में टकराव होता है, तो संसद द्वारा बनाया गया कानून प्रभावी होता है (अनुच्छेद 254)। शिक्षा को मूल रूप से राज्य सूची में रखा गया था, लेकिन 42वें संविधान संशोधन (1976) के द्वारा इसे समवर्ती सूची में स्थानांतरित कर दिया गया। इससे केंद्र को शिक्षा नीतियों को एकरूपता प्रदान करने का अधिकार मिला।

Extra Facts:
समवर्ती सूची में कुल 52 विषय शामिल हैं, जिनमें शिक्षा, विवाह और तलाक, दंड प्रक्रिया, वन, श्रम कल्याण आदि शामिल हैं। राज्य सूची में 61 विषय हैं, जबकि संघ सूची में 97 विषय हैं। शिक्षा का अधिकार अधिनियम (RTE), 2009 केंद्र सरकार द्वारा बनाया गया एक महत्वपूर्ण कानून है, जो 6-14 वर्ष के बच्चों को मुफ्त और अनिवार्य शिक्षा प्रदान करता है। यह अनुच्छेद 21A के तहत प्रदत्त मौलिक अधिकार को लागू करता है।

question:
Articles ___________ in Part VI of the Constitution deals with the organisation, composition, duration, officers, procedures, privileges, powers and so on of the state legislature.

[SSC GD 2022]
options: 158 to 200
150 to 212
168 to 212
150 to 168
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 168 to 212

Explanation:
Articles 168 to 212 in Part VI of the Indian Constitution deal with the provisions related to the State Legislature, including its organization, composition of Legislative Assembly and Council, qualifications of members, officers, legislative procedures, privileges, and powers. For example:
- Article 168 specifies the composition of the State Legislature.
- Article 169 outlines the process for the creation or abolition of the Legislative Council.
- Article 194 defines the privileges and immunities of legislators.

Extra Facts:
- While Articles 168–212 cover the State Legislature, the Parliament (Central Legislature) is governed by Articles 79–122.
- States with a Legislative Council have a bicameral system, while others are unicameral.
- Article 170 sets the maximum (500) and minimum (60) strength of the Legislative Assembly.

question_hi:
संविधान के भाग VI में अनुच्छेद ____________ राज्य विधायिका के संगठन, संरचना, अवधि, अधिकारियों, प्रक्रियाओं, विशेषाधिकारों, शक्तियों आदि से संबंधित हैं।

150 से 168
solution_hi:

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के भाग VI में अनुच्छेद 168 से 212 तक राज्य विधायिका (State Legislature) से संबंधित प्रावधान दिए गए हैं। इन अनुच्छेदों में राज्य विधानमंडल के संगठन, विधानसभा और विधान परिषद की संरचना, सदस्यों की योग्यताएँ, अधिकारी, विधायी प्रक्रिया, विशेषाधिकार, शक्तियाँ आदि शामिल हैं। उदाहरण के लिए:
- अनुच्छेद 168 राज्य विधानमंडल के गठन से संबंधित है।
- अनुच्छेद 169 विधान परिषद के सृजन या उन्मूलन की प्रक्रिया बताता है।
- अनुच्छेद 194 विधायकों के विशेषाधिकारों और उन्मुक्तियों को परिभाषित करता है।

Extra Facts:
- भारतीय संविधान में राज्य विधानमंडल का उल्लेख अनुच्छेद 168 से 212 तक किया गया है, जबकि संसद (केंद्रीय विधायिका) के लिए अनुच्छेद 79 से 122 तक प्रावधान हैं।
- विधान परिषद वाले राज्यों में द्विसदनीय व्यवस्था (Bicameral) होती है, जबकि अन्य राज्यों में एकसदनीय (Unicameral) व्यवस्था होती है।
- अनुच्छेद 170 विधानसभा की संरचना और सदस्यों की अधिकतम संख्या (500) तथा न्यूनतम संख्या (60) निर्धारित करता है।

question:
The Parliament does not have the power to legislate on the subjects in List 2 of the Seventh Schedule. Which of the following is an EXCEPTION to this general law?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: If the Judiciary asks the parliament to do so.
If the Prime Minister asks the Parliament to do so.
If the Governor of the state certifies the requirement.
If the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution to this effect.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is If the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution to this effect.

Explanation:
Under Article 249 of the Indian Constitution, if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by a two-thirds majority of members present and voting, the Parliament gains the power to legislate on subjects in the State List (List 2). This provision is invoked when a matter becomes of national importance. Thus, it is an exception to the general rule that Parliament cannot legislate on State List subjects.

Extra Facts:
- Article 249 is used when a subject gains national significance, such as during emergencies.
- Additionally, under Article 252, if two or more states request Parliament to make laws for them, Parliament can legislate on that subject.
- The Rajya Sabha is given this special power because it represents the states and plays a crucial role in maintaining federal balance.

question_hi:
संसद के पास भारतीय संविधान की अनुसूची सात की सूची 2 में शामिल विषयों पर कानून बनाने की शक्ति नहीं है। निम्नलिखित विकल्पों में से कौन सा इस सामान्य नियम का एक अपवाद है?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi: यदि न्यायपालिका संसद से ऐसा करने के लिए कहती है।
यदि प्रधान मंत्री संसद से ऐसा करने के लिए कहते हैं।
यदि राज्य के राज्यपाल इसकी आवश्यकता को प्रमाणित करते हैं।
यदि राज्य सभा इस आशय का प्रस्ताव पारित करती है।
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है यदि राज्य सभा इस आशय का प्रस्ताव पारित करती है।

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 249 के तहत, यदि राज्य सभा उपस्थित और मतदान करने वाले सदस्यों के दो-तिहाई बहुमत से एक प्रस्ताव पारित करती है, तो संसद को राज्य सूची (सूची 2) के विषयों पर कानून बनाने का अधिकार मिल जाता है। यह प्रावधान राष्ट्रीय हित में आवश्यक होने पर लागू किया जाता है। इस प्रकार, यह सामान्य नियम का एक अपवाद है कि संसद राज्य सूची के विषयों पर कानून नहीं बना सकती।

Extra Facts:
- अनुच्छेद 249 का उपयोग संसद द्वारा तब किया जाता है जब कोई विषय राष्ट्रीय महत्व का हो जाता है, जैसे कि आपातकालीन स्थितियों में।
- इसके अलावा, अनुच्छेद 252 के तहत, यदि दो या अधिक राज्य संसद से अपने लिए कानून बनाने का अनुरोध करते हैं, तो संसद उस विषय पर कानून बना सकती है।
- राज्य सभा को यह विशेष शक्ति इसलिए दी गई है क्योंकि यह राज्यों का प्रतिनिधित्व करती है और संघीय संतुलन बनाए रखने में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाती है।

question:
Which Chapter of Part VI of the Indian Constitution is concerned with the State Legislatures?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: Chapter II
Chapter III
Chapter V
Chapter VII
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Chapter III

Explanation:
Part VI of the Indian Constitution deals with the organization and functioning of state governments. Chapter III of this part specifically pertains to State Legislatures. It covers Articles 168 to 212, detailing the composition, powers, functions, and procedures of State Legislatures. This chapter includes provisions related to the Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) and Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad), qualifications of members, sessions, legislative processes, etc.

Extra Facts:
◼ Article 168 provides for the constitution of State Legislatures.
◼ Article 169 outlines the procedure for the creation or abolition of a Legislative Council.
◼ Article 170 defines the composition and number of members in the Legislative Assembly.
◼ Article 171 specifies the election and nomination process for Legislative Council members.
◼ Article 172 determines the duration of State Legislatures.

question:
Which of the following is related to the concurrent list of the seventh schedule of the Indian constitution?

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options: Taxes on agricultural income
Tolls
Factories
Taxes on income other than agricultural income.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Factories

Explanation:
The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains three lists: Union List (List I), State List (List II), and Concurrent List (List III). The Concurrent List includes subjects on which both Central and State governments can legislate. Factories fall under the Concurrent List (Entry 24), while the other options belong to different lists:
☛ Taxes on agricultural income → State List (Entry 46)
☛ Tolls → State List (Entry 59)
☛ Taxes on income other than agricultural income → Union List (Entry 82)

Extra Facts:
☛ The Union List has 97 subjects (originally 100), the State List has 66 subjects (originally 61), and the Concurrent List has 47 subjects (originally 52).
☛ In case of conflicts, the Union List prevails (Article 246).
☛ Key subjects like Education, Forests, and Labour Welfare are also part of the Concurrent List.

question:
The Constitution divided the powers between the Centre and the States in the terms of_________lists.

[RRC GROUP D]
options:
4

3

2

5
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 3

Explanation:
The Indian Constitution divides powers between the Centre and the States into three lists:
1. Union List (Article 246 & Seventh Schedule): Contains 98 subjects on which only the Central Government can legislate (e.g., defense, foreign affairs, banking).
2. State List: Includes 59 subjects under the jurisdiction of State Governments (e.g., police, public health, local governance).
3. Concurrent List: Covers 52 subjects where both Centre and States can make laws, but Central law prevails in case of conflict (Article 254).

Extra Facts:
- Residuary Powers (Article 248) lie with the Centre for subjects not mentioned in any list.
- The 42nd Amendment (1976) transferred five subjects from the State List to the Concurrent List (education, forests, etc.).
- The GST Council is a unique federal body to decide on GST-related matters, reflecting cooperative federalism.

question:
Central Bureau of Intelligence and Investigation comes under which list of the seventh schedule of the Indian constitution ?

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options: Union list
Concurrent list
State list
Transferred list
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Union list

Explanation:
The Central Bureau of Intelligence and Investigation (CBI) comes under the Union List (List I) of the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution. The Union List contains subjects on which only the Central Government has the power to legislate. The Seventh Schedule consists of three lists: Union List (List I), State List (List II), and Concurrent List (List III). The CBI was established under the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946 and operates under the Ministry of Home Affairs. Entry 8 of the Union List includes 'Central Bureau of Intelligence and Investigation,' under which the CBI derives its authority.

Extra Facts:
1. The Seventh Schedule currently has 100 subjects in the Union List, 61 in the State List, and 52 in the Concurrent List.
2. The CBI has jurisdiction over corruption cases, economic offenses, and special crimes.
3. The CBI cannot investigate in a state without the consent of the State Government, unless directed by the Supreme Court or High Court.
4. Both Central and State Governments can legislate on Concurrent List subjects, but in case of conflict, the Central law prevails.

question:
Which of the following comes under the 5th schedule of the Indian constitution?

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options: Provisions related to Schedule Areas and Scheduled Tribes
Provisions related to Tribal areas in states of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram
Provisions related to Oaths or Affirmations
Provisions related to Languages
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Provisions related to Schedule Areas and Scheduled Tribes

Explanation:
The Fifth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes. It falls under Article 244(1) and primarily concerns the management of Scheduled Areas in various states (Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan, and Telangana). It also mentions the formation and functions of the Tribal Advisory Council (TAC).

Extra Facts:
• The Sixth Schedule pertains to the administration of tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram (Article 244(2) and Article 275(1)).
• The Third Schedule relates to oaths and affirmations.
• The Eighth Schedule lists India's 22 officially recognized languages.

भाषाओं से संबंधित उपबंध
solution_hi:

Explanation:

question:
Which of the following is a feature of the Indian Constitution?

[SSC CHSL 2023]
options: Lengthiest written constitution
Rigid constitution
Presidential form of government
Dual citizenship
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lengthiest written constitution

Explanation:
The Indian Constitution is the lengthiest written constitution in the world, currently containing 395 articles, 12 schedules, and 105 amendments. It incorporates both federal and unitary features. Among the other options, 'Rigid constitution' is incorrect because the Indian Constitution has both rigid and flexible provisions. 'Presidential form of government' is wrong as India follows a parliamentary system, not a presidential one. 'Dual citizenship' is also incorrect because India provides for single citizenship (Articles 5-11).

Extra Facts:

☛ It took 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days to draft the Constitution.
☛ Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the President of the Constituent Assembly, while Dr. B.R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.
☛ The words 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' were added to the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment (1976).

States in part B of the first schedule
Armed forces in states in part A of the second schedule
Reservation for Anglo - Indian communities in parliament
solution:

Explanation:
Part VII of the Indian Constitution originally dealt with 'Part B States' (States listed in Part B of the First Schedule). These were former princely states integrated into the Indian Union. question:
Part XVI of the Indian constitution deals with___________

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Elections
Special provisions related to certain classes
Constitutional amendments

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Special provisions related to certain classes

Explanation:
Part XVI (Articles 330-342) of the Indian Constitution deals with 'Special provisions related to certain classes', including Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), and the Anglo-Indian community. It provides reservations for these groups in the Lok Sabha (Article 330) and State Legislative Assemblies (Article 332). Article 338 establishes the National Commission for Scheduled Castes, while Article 338A creates the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes. This part reinforces the Constitution's principles of social justice and equality.

Extra Facts:
• Article 341 empowers the President to notify the list of Scheduled Castes.
• Article 342 empowers the President to notify the list of Scheduled Tribes.
• The 104th Constitutional Amendment (2019) abolished reservations for Anglo-Indians in Lok Sabha and State Assemblies.
• Article 335 allows reservations in government jobs for SCs/STs while maintaining administrative efficiency.

question:
In the Constitution of India, Part IV A deals with the:

[NTPC CBT 2]
options: Fundamental Rights
Fundamental Duties
Directive Principles of State Policy
Citizenship
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Fundamental Duties

Explanation:
Part IV A of the Indian Constitution deals with Fundamental Duties, which were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976) based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee. These duties are enshrined under Article 51A and list 11 duties for citizens, including respecting the Constitution, national flag, and anthem, promoting harmony, and developing a scientific temper. Although these duties are not enforceable by courts, they hold constitutional significance.

Extra Facts:
- Fundamental Duties were inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.
- The 86th Constitutional Amendment (2002) added a new duty, making it obligatory for parents/guardians to provide education to children aged 6-14 years.
- The Verma Committee (1999) recommended measures to make Fundamental Duties more effective.

question:
Which Schedule of the Constitution of India deals with Union, State and Concurrent lists?

[SSC GD 2022]
options: 11th
9th
7th
5th
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 7th

Explanation:
The 7th Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the Union List, State List, and Concurrent List. It is defined under Article 246 and divides legislative powers between the Centre and States.
- Union List (List I): Contains 98 subjects on which only Parliament can legislate (e.g., defence, foreign affairs).
- State List (List II): Includes 59 subjects under the jurisdiction of State Legislatures (e.g., police, local government).
- Concurrent List (List III): Covers 52 subjects where both Centre and States can make laws (e.g., education, marriage).

Extra Facts:
- Under Article 248, Parliament has exclusive power over residual subjects (e.g., computer software).
- The 42nd Amendment (1976) transferred several subjects (e.g., education, forests) from the State List to the Concurrent List.
- In Goa vs Union of India (1982), the Supreme Court ruled that in case of a conflict, the Union List prevails over the State List.

question:
Which of the following schedules of the Constitution of India has been INCORRECTLY matched with its content?

Explanation:
The Second Schedule of the Indian Constitution does not mention languages; instead, it deals with salaries, allowances, and privileges of constitutional functionaries like the President, Governors, Judges of SC/HC, etc. Languages are listed in the Eighth Schedule (22 languages). - Fourth Schedule: Allocation of Rajya Sabha seats to states.

Extra Facts:

- Key schedules: Seventh Schedule (Union, State, Concurrent Lists), Ninth Schedule (laws immune to judicial review), and Twelfth Schedule (municipalities’ functions).
- The 52nd Amendment Act (1985) added the Tenth Schedule (anti-defection law).

question:
Articles 245 to 255 in Part XI of the Indian Constitution deal with the ____________.

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: emergency provisions
financial relations between the Centre and the states
legislative relations between the Centre and the states
tribunals
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is legislative relations between the Centre and the states

Explanation:
Part XI (Articles 245-255) of the Indian Constitution deals with legislative relations between the Centre and the states. This part defines the distribution of legislative powers between the Union and States, covering the Union List, State List, and Concurrent List. Article 245 determines the legislative jurisdiction of Parliament and State Legislatures, while Article 246 distributes subjects among the three lists. This section strengthens the federal structure of India.

Extra Facts:
- Article 248 grants Parliament the power to legislate on residual subjects.
- Article 249 allows Parliament to legislate on State List subjects in the national interest if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by a two-thirds majority.
- Article 252 empowers Parliament to make laws for two or more states upon their request.
- Article 254 gives precedence to Central laws in case of inconsistency with State laws.

question:
The Indian Constitution originally consisted of how many Articles?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: 395
595
345
495
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 395

Explanation:
The Indian Constitution was originally adopted on 26th November 1949 with 395 Articles, divided into 22 Parts and 8 Schedules. The Constituent Assembly took 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days to draft it. The original Constitution covered various subjects like citizenship, fundamental rights, directive principles, center-state relations, and judiciary under Articles 1 to 395. Over time, new Articles have been added through amendments, but the original count was 395.

Extra Facts:
- The Indian Constitution is the longest written constitution in the world.
- It currently has 470 Articles (in 25 Parts) and 12 Schedules.
- The Constituent Assembly held its final session on 24th January 1950, when members signed it.
- The Constitution came into force on 26th January 1950, celebrated as Republic Day.

question:
Which of the following do/does NOT come under the Union list of seventh schedule of the Indian constitution ?

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options: Intoxicating liquors
Post and telegraphs
Audit of the accounts of the states
Banking
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Intoxicating liquors

Explanation:
The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains three lists: Union List (List I), State List (List II), and Concurrent List (List III). The Union List includes subjects on which only the central government can legislate. Intoxicating liquors fall under the State List (List II) (under Article 47), whereas Post and telegraphs (Entry 31 of Union List), Audit of the accounts of the states (Entry 76 of Union List), and Banking (Entry 45 of Union List) are part of the Union List.

Extra Facts:
- The Seventh Schedule contains 97 subjects in the Union List, 66 subjects in the State List, and 47 subjects in the Concurrent List.
- Article 246 distributes legislative powers between Parliament and State Legislatures.
- Parliament can legislate on certain State List subjects under special circumstances, such as in the national interest (Article 249) or during emergencies (Article 250).

Expected Questions for Upcoming Exams :
☛ Which schedule of the Indian Constitution contains Union, State, and Concurrent Lists? → Seventh Schedule
☛ How many subjects are in the Union List? → 97
☛ Which subject is included in the State List? → Police, Public Health
☛ Which subject is included in the Concurrent List? → Education, Marriage
☛ Under which article can Parliament legislate on a State List subject? → Article 249
question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा भारतीय संविधान की सातवीं अनुसूची की संघ सूची के अंतर्गत नहीं आता है?

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options_hi: नशीली शराब
डाक और तार
राज्यों के लेखाओं की संपरीक्षा
बैंकिंग
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है नशीली शराब

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान की सातवीं अनुसूची में तीन सूचियाँ हैं: संघ सूची (Union List), राज्य सूची (State List) और समवर्ती सूची (Concurrent List)। संघ सूची (List I) में वे विषय शामिल हैं जिन पर केवल केंद्र सरकार कानून बना सकती है। नशीली शराब (Intoxicating liquors) राज्य सूची (List II) के अंतर्गत आता है (अनुच्छेद 47 के तहत), जबकि डाक और तार (Post and telegraphs) (संघ सूची की प्रविष्टि 31), राज्यों के लेखाओं की संपरीक्षा (Audit of the accounts of the states) (संघ सूची की प्रविष्टि 76), और बैंकिंग (Banking) (संघ सूची की प्रविष्टि 45) संघ सूची में शामिल हैं।

Extra Facts:
- सातवीं अनुसूची में संघ सूची में 97 विषय, राज्य सूची में 66 विषय और समवर्ती सूची में 47 विषय शामिल हैं।
- अनुच्छेद 246 संसद और राज्य विधानमंडलों के बीच विधायी शक्तियों का वितरण करता है।
- राज्य सूची के कुछ विषयों पर संसद विशेष परिस्थितियों में कानून बना सकती है, जैसे राष्ट्रीय हित में (अनुच्छेद 249) या आपातकाल के दौरान (अनुच्छेद 250)।

Expected Questions for Upcoming Exams :
☛ भारतीय संविधान की किस अनुसूची में संघ, राज्य और समवर्ती सूचियाँ हैं? → सातवीं अनुसूची
☛ संघ सूची में कितने विषय हैं? → 97
☛ राज्य सूची में कौन सा विषय शामिल है? → पुलिस, सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य
☛ समवर्ती सूची में कौन सा विषय शामिल है? → शिक्षा, विवाह
☛ किस अनुच्छेद के तहत संसद राज्य सूची के विषय पर कानून बना सकती है? → अनुच्छेद 249

question:
Provisions as to disqualification on ground of defection are mentioned under which schedule of the Indian constitution?

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options: 12th schedule
11th schedule
10th schedule
9th schedule
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 10th Schedule

Explanation:
The 10th Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains provisions regarding disqualification on the grounds of defection. It was added by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985. This schedule aims to prevent legislators from switching political parties arbitrarily. If a member votes against their party's directive or voluntarily leaves the party, they can be disqualified. The provisions are linked to Articles 102(2) and 191(2), which deal with the disqualification of MPs and MLAs, respectively.

Extra Facts:
- The 10th Schedule is popularly known as the 'Anti-Defection Law'.
- Its objective is to maintain party discipline and ensure government stability.
- The 91st Constitutional Amendment (2003) tightened defection rules, allowing only mergers with a two-thirds majority of legislators to avoid disqualification.
- The decision on defection cases lies with the Speaker/Chairman of the House, subject to judicial review (Kihoto Hollohan Case, 1992).

Expected Questions for Upcoming Exams :
☛ Which constitutional amendment introduced the Anti-Defection Law? → 52nd Amendment (1985)
☛ What is the 10th Schedule related to? → Disqualification on grounds of defection
☛ Who decides defection cases? → Speaker/Chairman of the House
☛ What change did the 91st Amendment bring? → Stricter anti-defection rules
☛ Which case held that the Speaker’s decision is subject to judicial review? → Kihoto Hollohan Case (1992)
question_hi:
भारतीय संविधान की किस अनुसूची में दल-बदल के आधार पर अयोग्यता के प्रावधानों का उल्लेख किया गया है?

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options_hi: 12 वीं अनुसूची
11 वीं अनुसूची
10 वीं अनुसूची
9वीं अनुसूची
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है 10 वीं अनुसूची

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान की 10 वीं अनुसूची में दल-बदल (Defection) के आधार पर अयोग्यता के प्रावधानों का उल्लेख किया गया है। इसे 1985 में 52वें संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम द्वारा जोड़ा गया था। यह अनुसूची संसद और राज्य विधानमंडलों के सदस्यों को दल-बदल करने से रोकने के लिए बनाई गई है। यदि कोई सदस्य अपने राजनीतिक दल के निर्देश के विरुद्ध मतदान करता है या दल छोड़ता है, तो उसे अयोग्य घोषित किया जा सकता है। इसके अंतर्गत अनुच्छेद 102(2) और 191(2) में संसद और राज्य विधानसभाओं के सदस्यों की अयोग्यता का प्रावधान है।

Extra Facts:
- 10वीं अनुसूची को 'दल-बदल विरोधी कानून' (Anti-Defection Law) के नाम से भी जाना जाता है।
- इस कानून का उद्देश्य राजनीतिक दलों में अनुशासन बनाए रखना और सरकार की स्थिरता सुनिश्चित करना है।
- 91वें संविधान संशोधन (2003) ने दल-बदल के नियमों को और सख्त बनाया, जिसमें दो-तिहाई सदस्यों के समूह द्वारा विलय को छोड़कर किसी भी दल-बदल को अयोग्यता का आधार बनाया गया।
- दल-बदल के मामलों का निर्णय सदन के अध्यक्ष/सभापति द्वारा किया जाता है, जिसे न्यायिक समीक्षा के दायरे में रखा गया है (किहोतो होलोहन मामला, 1992)।

Expected Questions for Upcoming Exams :

☛ 10वीं अनुसूची का संबंध किससे है? → दल-बदल के आधार पर अयोग्यता
☛ दल-बदल के मामलों में निर्णय लेने का अधिकार किसे है? → सदन के अध्यक्ष/सभापति
☛ 91वें संविधान संशोधन ने क्या बदलाव किया? → दल-बदल नियमों को सख्त बनाया
☛ किस मामले में SC ने कहा कि अध्यक्ष का निर्णय न्यायिक समीक्षा के अधीन है? → किहोतो होलोहन मामला (1992)

question:
Which Part of the Constitution of India deals with the powers and functioning of the Supreme Court of India?

[SSC GD 2022]
options: Part V
Part VI
Part X
Part XI
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Part V

Explanation:
Part V of the Indian Constitution deals with the Union and includes Articles 124 to 147, which elaborate on the powers, functioning, appointment and removal of judges, jurisdiction, etc. of the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court is the highest judicial authority in India and also the guardian of the Constitution. It has original, appellate, and advisory jurisdictions. Under Article 32, the Supreme Court can issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.

Extra Facts:
The Supreme Court was established on 28th January 1950. Its first Chief Justice was Harilal J. Kania. The retirement age of Supreme Court judges is 65 years. In the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), the Supreme Court established the Doctrine of Basic Structure of the Constitution. To remove a Supreme Court judge, a motion must be passed by a special majority in both Houses of Parliament.

question_hi:
भारत के संविधान का कौन सा भाग भारत के सर्वोच्च न्यायालय की शक्तियों और कार्यप्रणाली से संबंधित है?

[SSC GD 2022]
options_hi: भाग V
भाग VI
भाग X
भाग XI
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है भाग V

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का भाग V संघ से संबंधित है और इसके अंतर्गत अनुच्छेद 124 से 147 तक सर्वोच्च न्यायालय की शक्तियों, कार्यप्रणाली, न्यायाधीशों की नियुक्ति, हटाने की प्रक्रिया, अधिकार क्षेत्र आदि का विस्तृत वर्णन किया गया है। सर्वोच्च न्यायालय भारत का सर्वोच्च न्यायिक प्राधिकरण है और यह संविधान का संरक्षक भी है। इसके पास मूल, अपीलीय और सलाहकारी अधिकार क्षेत्र हैं। अनुच्छेद 32 के तहत सर्वोच्च न्यायालय मौलिक अधिकारों के प्रवर्तन के लिए रिट जारी कर सकता है।

Extra Facts:
सर्वोच्च न्यायालय की स्थापना 28 जनवरी, 1950 को हुई थी। इसके प्रथम मुख्य न्यायाधीश हरिलाल जे. कनिया थे। सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के न्यायाधीशों की सेवानिवृत्ति की आयु 65 वर्ष है। केसवानंद भारती मामले (1973) में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने संविधान के मूल ढांचे के सिद्धांत को स्थापित किया था। सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के न्यायाधीशों को हटाने के लिए संसद के दोनों सदनों द्वारा विशेष बहुमत से प्रस्ताव पारित किया जाना आवश्यक है।
